tEn: Politics Gets Interested In Those Trying Not To Die
tZh: 政治开始关注那些试图不死的人
sEn: The government blocks AI labs from coordinating on safety while threatening antitrust action, preventing voluntary cooperation to avoid dangerous superintelligence.
sZh: 政府一边阻止 AI 实验室在安全问题上协调，一边威胁反垄断，从而阻止了为避免危险超级智能而进行的自愿合作。
absEn: This article examines the political and regulatory landscape surrounding AI development, focusing on the Trump administration's contradictory stance toward AI safety. It argues that while the White House publicly dismisses existential AI risk as a 'hoax,' it simultaneously imposes mandatory safety reviews and ad hoc interventions, such as forcing models offline. The core tension lies in the government's refusal to address collective action problems: it blocks labs from coordinating on safety while threatening antitrust action, effectively preventing voluntary cooperation to avoid building dangerous superintelligence. The author concludes that the government is actively obstructing the very coordination needed to prevent catastrophe, prioritizing business interests and political posturing over meaningful safeguards. The situation is dire but not hopeless, as some officials acknowledge the need for sane responses, though progress remains far too slow.
absZh: 本文考察围绕 AI 发展的政治与监管格局，聚焦特朗普政府在 AI 安全上的矛盾立场。文章指出，白宫一方面公开将 AI 生存风险斥为“骗局”，另一方面却强制实施安全审查并采取临时干预措施，例如强制模型下线。核心矛盾在于政府拒绝解决集体行动问题：它阻止实验室在安全上协调，同时威胁反垄断行动，实际上阻止了为避免构建危险超级智能而进行的自愿合作。作者得出结论：政府正在积极阻碍防止灾难所需的那种协调，将商业利益和政治作秀置于有意义的保障之上。局势严峻但并非无望，因为一些官员承认需要理性的应对，尽管进展仍远远太慢。

full.sec: The American People Really Hate AI
full.secZh: 美国民众确实讨厌 AI

paras.en: If Americans understood that Trump was calling not only existential risk from AI but also every complaint involving data centers one of his 'hoaxes,' I would expect his approval rating here, and overall, to deteriorate rather further.
paras.zh: 如果美国人明白，特朗普不仅把 AI 带来的生存性风险、还把一切涉及数据中心的抱怨都称作他的“骗局”，那么我预计他在这一问题上的支持率，乃至整体支持率，都会进一步下滑。

paras.en: I would extend this even further if you include the things I did not know about when I wrote the above sentence, because at the time it was only Friday. Life comes at you fast.
paras.zh: 如果把我在写下上面那句话时还不知道的事情也算进去，我还会把这一点推得更远，因为当时才只是周五。生活变化得真快。

paras.en: Anyway, this was the situation in a poll published last week. His overall approval is included for context:
paras.zh: 总之，这就是上周公布的一项民调中的情况。为便于参照，这里也附上了他的整体支持率：

paras.en: Trump thinks the problem is not saying his positions clearly or loudly enough, and he is going to try and fix that. Did you know there is an election in six weeks?
paras.zh: 特朗普认为问题在于他的立场表达得不够清楚、不够响亮，他打算设法解决这一点。你知道六周后就要举行选举了吗？

paras.en: On September 19, around 10:12am, he dropped this new creation, only modified to include paragraph breaks since Trump thinks the enter key is a HOAX.
paras.zh: 9 月 19 日上午 10 点 12 分左右，他发布了这个新作品，仅修改以包含段落分隔，因为特朗普认为回车键是一个骗局。

paras.en: Donald Trump: Over the years, there have been many Hoaxes, all generated by the Radical Left Dumocrats, for purposes of destroying our Country. RUSSIA, RUSSIA, RUSSIA, UKRAINE, UKRAINE, UKRAINE, Global Warming, Impeachment Hoax #1, Impeachment Hoax #2, Men in Women’s Sports, Transgender for Everyone,
paras.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普：多年来，有许多骗局，都是激进左翼民主党人制造的，目的是摧毁我们的国家。俄罗斯，俄罗斯，俄罗斯，乌克兰，乌克兰，乌克兰，全球变暖，弹劾骗局#1，弹劾骗局#2，男性参加女子体育运动，跨性别者人人平等，

paras.en: and now, the decimation, or destruction, of AI, commonly known as Artificial Intelligence — And I, as President of the United States, will not stand by and let this happen.
paras.zh: 而现在，是人工智能（通常称为 AI）的毁灭或破坏——而我，作为美国总统，不会袖手旁观，让这种事情发生。

paras.en: It all began with an attack on our Data Centers, until people realized how wealthy and prestigious they were for the Communities in which they were built. Higher Salaries, Lower Taxes, and Safer Streets, was the result, and the crazed Data Center attack has largely failed, so now, in much the same way as they changed the term “Global Warming” to “Climate Change,” in that it covers a much larger “territory” of doubt, they are going straight at AI.
paras.zh: 这一切始于对我们数据中心的攻击，直到人们意识到这些数据中心对所在社区来说是多么富有和有声望。更高的薪水、更低的税收和更安全的街道就是结果，而疯狂的数据中心攻击基本上失败了，所以现在，就像他们将“全球变暖”一词改为“气候变化”一样，因为它涵盖了更大的“怀疑领域”，他们正直接针对 AI。

paras.en: Trump has come a long way with the tactic of calling things failures in order to cause them to fail. There is no world in which the ‘crazed Data Center attack’ has largely failed, and if it had we wouldn’t be here talking about it this way.
paras.zh: 特朗普在将事情称为失败以导致其失败方面已经走了很长一段路。‘疯狂的数据中心攻击’基本上失败的情况根本不存在，如果它失败了，我们就不会在这里这样谈论它。

paras.en: We will not in any way hinder or stifle the growth of this incredible industry. Rather, we will cherish it, help it, and watch over it, as it grows! However, we will also be looking for BAD, and we can do that, very easily, with our already existing Criminal and Civil Justice System.
paras.zh: 我们绝不会以任何方式阻碍或扼杀这个不可思议的行业的发展。相反，我们会珍视它、帮助它，并在它成长的过程中守护它！然而，我们也会寻找“坏”的东西，而且我们可以非常容易地做到这一点，利用我们已有的刑事和民事司法系统。

paras.en: As in, no new rules or regulations, except the ones I already added, and the ones I ad hoc add later when I feel like it because I think something is bad. And by bad I mean bad for business.
paras.zh: 也就是说，没有新的规则或法规，除了我已经添加的，以及我以后心血来潮时临时添加的，因为我觉得某些东西是坏的。而所谓的坏，我指的是对商业不利。

paras.en: For this purpose, I am forming the AI Force, much like I did Space Force, which has been a tremendous SUCCESS, in my First Term. To that end, I will be announcing, in the near future, the AI “Czar” — Only High I.Q. individuals need apply!
paras.zh: 为此，我正在组建 AI 部队，就像我在第一任期内组建的太空部队一样，那是一个巨大的成功。为此，我将在不久的将来宣布 AI“沙皇”——只有高智商的人才能申请！

paras.en: Hey, I like to think of myself as a High I.Q. individual.
paras.zh: 嘿，我喜欢把自己看作一个高智商的人。

paras.en: David Sacks was the first AI Czar, so it would be hard but not impossible to do worse.
paras.zh: 大卫·萨克斯是第一位 AI 沙皇，所以要做得更差很难，但并非不可能。

paras.en: The more interesting idea is the AI Force. It actually is plausible that the Space Force is a success, as far as it goes. What would it mean to have an AI Force? Who knows. Could be anything. The analogy to Space Force does not actually make logistical sense, nor does having a branch of the military. I can think of versions called AI Force that are net useful and sane. I can think of versions that are neither.
paras.zh: 更有趣的想法是 AI Force（人工智能部队）。就目前而言，太空军取得成功确实是可能的。拥有一支 AI Force 意味着什么？谁知道呢。什么都可能。与太空军类比在后勤上其实并不合理，设立一个军种分支也同样不合理。我能想到一些名为 AI Force 的版本，是净有用且理性的。我也能想到一些两者皆非的版本。

paras.en: AI is the next Industrial Revolution, or Internet, but will be even larger and more impactful, possibly as much as 25% of our Country's GDP. We are leading China, and the rest of the World, and I intend to keep it that way!
paras.zh: AI 是下一场工业革命，或者互联网，但规模会更大、影响会更深远，可能高达我国 GDP 的 25%。我们正领先于中国以及世界其他地区，我打算保持这一优势！

paras.en: He's a quarter of the way there. AI could be as much as 100% of our Country's GDP.
paras.zh: 他已经完成了四分之一。AI 可能高达我国 GDP 的 100%。

paras.en: Trump also decided to… rename AI? The man does have a knack for names.
paras.zh: 特朗普还决定……重新命名 AI？这家伙确实有起名字的天赋。

paras.en: Donald J. Trump: Many people think that the words “Artificial Intelligence” are inaccurate, and very ineloquent, relative to AI, or Artificial Intelligence. A far more elegant and accurate description of this new phenomenon would be Superior Intelligence (SI) or, Extreme Intelligence (EI) or, Supreme Intelligence (SI). This is a Poll, and I would appreciate everybody voting! Which is the best name for this ever growing “Revolution?” President DONALD J. TRUMP
paras.zh: 唐纳德·J·特朗普：许多人认为“人工智能”这个词不准确，而且相对于 AI 或 Artificial Intelligence 来说非常不文雅。对这种新现象，一个更优雅、更准确的描述应该是“高级智能”（Superior Intelligence，SI）或“极端智能”（Extreme Intelligence，EI）或“至高智能”（Supreme Intelligence，SI）。这是一项投票，我希望大家都能投票！对于这场不断发展的“革命”，哪个名字最好？唐纳德·J·特朗普总统

paras.en: Of the three, all of which are funny, Superior Intelligence is the best. None of them make sense for obvious reasons if you try saying them in a sentence, but that’s okay.
paras.zh: 在这三个名字中，虽然都很有趣，但“高级智能”是最好的。如果你试着把它们用在句子里，由于显而易见的原因，它们都说不通，但没关系。

paras.en: Then he decided ‘supreme’ is bad because of the ‘supreme court’ and reset the vote:
paras.zh: 然后他认为“至高”不好，因为“最高法院”的缘故，于是重新设置了投票：

paras.en: Donald J. Trump: “Supreme Intelligence,” probably because of its relationship to the Supreme Court, is losing badly to both “Superior” and “Extreme Intelligence.” Therefore, we are going to take “Supreme Intelligence” OUT, deleting it as a qualifier, and let you vote for the Final Two: Superior Intelligence, or Extreme Intelligence. A fresh Vote begins now!
paras.zh: 唐纳德·J·特朗普：“至高智能”可能因为与最高法院有关联，目前远远落后于“高级智能”和“极端智能”。因此，我们将把“至高智能”剔除，删除这个选项，让大家在最后两个选项中投票：高级智能，还是极端智能。新一轮投票现在开始！

paras.en: It’s weird to see such random outright falsehoods, since Supreme Intelligence was actually outright ahead of Extreme at the time he said it was ‘losing badly’ to it, but whatever, do we even notice such things anymore, nothing matters, etc.
paras.zh: 看到如此随意的 outright 谎言真是奇怪，因为 Supreme Intelligence 实际上在当时 outright 领先于 Extreme，而他说它“惨败”给 Extreme，但无所谓，我们还会注意到这种事吗，什么都不重要了，等等。

paras.en: I’m not sure if that was before or after he announced the new plan for a Triumphal Arch that will double as a military complex.
paras.zh: 我不确定那是在他宣布凯旋门新计划之前还是之后，该计划将兼作军事综合体。

paras.en: Never one to believe the polls, or not tempt fate, Trump went a different way.
paras.zh: 特朗普从不相信民调，也不愿冒险，他选择了不同的方式。

paras.en: Andrew Curran: President Trump just now on Truth Social:
paras.zh: Andrew Curran：特朗普总统刚才在 Truth Social 上表示：

paras.en: ‘I’m not going to stifle Growth, of something that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution, or the Internet, itself. We will be careful, and that’s why we have the Department of Justice, and other Law Enforcement bodies, that will rein things in if we have to, but I will only encourage AI or, SI (SUPER INTELLIGENCE)!
paras.zh: “我不会扼杀增长，这种增长将比工业革命或互联网本身更大。我们会小心谨慎，这就是为什么我们有司法部和其他执法机构，必要时他们会加以控制，但我只会鼓励 AI 或 SI（超级智能）！”

paras.en: This bit of 'oh, we will use the existing criminal law to deal with AI threats' is absurdist. I would presume that by 'SUPER INTELLIGENCE' he does not mean superintelligence as we talk about it here, and instead simply means AI is super, the same way Zuckerberg says superintelligence means his new AI glasses.
paras.zh: “哦，我们会用现有刑法来应对 AI 威胁”这种说法简直是荒诞主义。我推测，他所说的“SUPER INTELLIGENCE”并非我们这里讨论的超级智能，而只是指 AI 很超级，就像扎克伯格说超级智能指的是他的新 AI 眼镜一样。

paras.en: I wonder if Trump even knows that this name was 'taken' or the confusions this will bring. It's possible he knew and did it on purpose on several levels. It is also possible he has no idea.
paras.zh: 我想知道特朗普是否知道这个名字已被“占用”，或者这会带来怎样的混乱。他可能知道，并且有意在多个层面上这么做。也有可能他完全不知情。

paras.en: The New York Times confirms that the dark triad is David Sacks, Jensen Huang and Mark Zuckerberg, warning him about ‘losing to China.’ It’s a little on the nose, but our writers this season are on increasingly tight deadlines so I sympathize.
paras.zh: 《纽约时报》证实，所谓“黑暗三人组”就是 David Sacks、Jensen Huang 和 Mark Zuckerberg，他们警告他“会输给中国”。这有点过于直白，但本季我们的作者截稿期限越来越紧，所以我表示同情。

paras.en: David E. Sanger, Jonathan Swan, Cecilia Kang and Dustin Volz (NYTimes): People who have discussed the subject with Mr. Trump in private say his outbursts are rooted in worries that if the artificial intelligence boom fueling the American economy slows down, the market could crash and recession could quickly follow.
paras.zh: David E. Sanger、Jonathan Swan、Cecilia Kang 和 Dustin Volz（《纽约时报》）：私下与特朗普先生讨论过此事的人说，他的情绪爆发源于担忧：如果推动美国经济的人工智能热潮放缓，市场可能崩溃，衰退可能随之迅速到来。

paras.en: I do get the concern, especially on the data center side. Maybe this is as simple as Trump not understanding that when Dario Amodei and Sam Altman say ‘slow down AI’ they mean ‘do not go into full recursive self-improvement and get ten times faster.’
paras.zh: 我确实理解这种担忧，尤其是在数据中心方面。也许事情很简单：特朗普不明白，当 Dario Amodei 和 Sam Altman 说“放慢 AI”时，他们的意思是“不要进入完全递归式自我改进、变得快十倍”。

paras.en: As always, hold your fire. Trump is unique and Republicans are otherwise coming around. Inside the White House, many are attempting to respond sanely.
paras.zh: 一如既往，先别开火。特朗普是独特的，而共和党人除此之外正在转变态度。在白宫内部，许多人正试图理性地回应。

paras.en: The more cautious tone inside the White House reflects a growing concern that despite the strategic challenge posed by China, a summer of A.I. surprises has raised the prospect of risks that were often dismissed a year ago as the wild talk of “doomers.”
paras.zh: 白宫内部更为谨慎的语调反映出一种日益增长的担忧：尽管中国构成了战略挑战，但一个夏天的人工智能意外事件已经提高了风险出现的可能性——而这些风险在一年前还常被斥为“末日论者”的疯狂言论。

paras.en: … Mr. Bessent and the White House chief of staff, Susie Wiles, have been increasingly concerned over the past several months that A.I. could cause massive disruptions across industries, including hacks into major financial institutions that could destabilize the world economy.
paras.zh: ……贝森特先生和白宫幕僚长苏西·威尔斯在过去几个月里越来越担心，人工智能可能对各行业造成大规模破坏，包括入侵大型金融机构，从而可能破坏世界经济稳定。

paras.en: Ms. Wiles this year began organizing an informal group to think about how to deal with the risk created by new, more powerful models.
paras.zh: 威尔斯女士今年开始组织一个非正式小组，思考如何应对新的、更强大的模型所带来的风险。

paras.en: Is the situation great? Oh, hell no. The situation is terrible.
paras.zh: 情况好吗？哦，当然不好。情况很糟糕。

paras.en: But it is not as terrible as it sounds. The goalposts have moved quite a bit.
paras.zh: 但情况并没有听起来那么糟糕。目标已经发生了相当大的变化。

paras.en: Consider that those getting ready for the US-China summit still hope for progress:
paras.zh: 考虑到那些为中美峰会做准备的人仍然希望取得进展：

paras.en: … But already, officials say, some of the most expansive ideas being discussed among A.I. safety experts, including an agreement on safety standards and reviews of forthcoming Chinese and American A.I. models before their public release, are unlikely to be part of any initial accord.
paras.zh: ……但官员们表示，人工智能安全专家正在讨论的一些最宏大的构想，包括就安全标准达成协议以及在即将推出的中美人工智能模型公开发布前对其进行审查，不太可能成为任何初步协议的一部分。

paras.en: One diplomat involved in the effort said he believed “the best we can hope for” is the creation of some kind of U.S.-China working group that might build on a Biden-era agreement with China to bar the use of artificial intelligence in decisions about the employment of nuclear weapons.
paras.zh: 一位参与这项努力的外交官表示，他认为“我们能期望的最好结果”是建立某种美中工作组，该工作组可能会以拜登时期与中国达成的协议为基础，禁止在核武器使用决策中使用人工智能。

paras.en: This is not what we would have hoped for, but this is moving forward, albeit way too slowly, rather than backward.
paras.zh: 这不是我们所希望的结果，但这是在向前推进，尽管速度太慢，而不是在倒退。

paras.en: The United States could go its own way and impose mandatory reviews of the safety of new, American-generated models, but Mr. Trump and his aides believe that would effectively drive the global market to Chinese largely open-source alternatives.
paras.zh: 美国可以走自己的路，对新的美国生成模型的安全性进行强制性审查，但特朗普先生及其助手认为，这实际上会将全球市场推向中国 largely 开源的替代方案。

paras.en: Trump literally already did go his own way and impose mandatory reviews of the safety of new, American-generated models.
paras.zh: 特朗普实际上已经走自己的路，并对新的美国生成模型的安全性实施了强制性审查。

paras.en: He imposed his 'voluntary' review framework for new model releases. No one thinks those reviews are voluntary. Not the labs, not the legal experts, not the market, and not the White House.
paras.zh: 他为新模型发布强加了一套“自愿”审查框架。没有人认为这些审查是自愿的。实验室不这么认为，法律专家不这么认为，市场不这么认为，白宫也不这么认为。

paras.en: If you want to know how not voluntary all of this is, we also have reports that when Trump was demanding Fable 5 be taken offline due to a supposed jailbreak demo, Trump said 'I want to send them to jail' if they refused to comply. Honestly, fair, and not a bombshell or anything like that. The rest of the associated Politico profile also echoed my previous understanding of the situation.
paras.zh: 如果你想知道这一切有多么不自愿，我们还有报道称，当 Trump 因一段所谓的越狱演示而要求将 Fable 5 下线时，Trump 表示如果他们拒绝服从，“我想把他们送进监狱”。说实话，这很合理，也算不上什么重磅消息之类的东西。相关 Politico 人物报道的其余部分也印证了我此前对局势的理解。

paras.en: As in, the President is both calling a 'hoax' on his own policies, and also saying he wants a fully ad hoc system where he alone decides what the rules are, on a case by case basis, rather than having a nation of laws. Since he is such a 'high IQ individual.'
paras.zh: 也就是说，总统既把自己制定的政策称为“骗局”，又表示他想要一个完全临时的体系，由他本人在个案基础上独自决定规则是什么，而不是一个法治国家。毕竟他是如此一位“高智商个体”。

full.sec: It’s All About the Data Centers

paras.en: David Sacks and his AI try to brag about all that AI has done for us, and come up with four things:
paras.zh: David Sacks 和他的 AI 试图吹嘘 AI 为我们所做的一切，并提出了四件事：

paras.en: David Sacks: Thanks to President Trump's leadership on AI:
paras.zh: David Sacks：感谢特朗普总统在 AI 方面的领导：

paras.en: — a million new jobs have been created around the AI buildout;
paras.zh: ——围绕 AI 建设已创造了 100 万个新工作岗位；

paras.en: Astra estimates at most 210,000 construction jobs from first principles.
paras.zh: Astra 从第一性原理出发估计，最多有 21 万个建筑工作岗位。

paras.en: Fable tracks the million claim down to The Economist from September 5, where there are 320,000 plausibly buildout-related jobs, and then they pile on 730,000 'above-trend' jobs for engineers, software developers, mathematicians (?!) and data scientists since 2022.
paras.zh: Fable 将百万岗位的说法追溯到 9 月 5 日的《经济学人》，其中约有 32 万个可能与建设相关的岗位，然后他们又加上了自 2022 年以来工程师、软件开发人员、数学家（？！）和数据科学家的 73 万个“高于趋势”的岗位。

paras.en: That’s not the buildout; it is trend selection, and it starts in 2022, not 2025 when Trump’s term started.
paras.zh: 那不是建设潮，而是趋势选择，而且它始于 2022 年，而非特朗普任期开始的 2025 年。

paras.en: — 401(k)s are up ~12% this year as AI capex and productivity lift the market;
paras.zh: —— 随着 AI 资本支出和生产率提振市场，401(k) 退休金账户今年上涨约 12%；

paras.en: Correlation is not causation, but Sacks is only claiming directional impact here. I actually do think this is causation versus no AI, and that the market would be down otherwise, but Sacks is not in a political position to point this out.
paras.zh: 相关性不等于因果性，但 Sacks 在此只主张方向性影响。我确实认为，相对于没有 AI 的情形，这就是因果关系，否则市场本会下跌，但 Sacks 并不处于指出这一点的政治位置。

paras.en: — America is re-industrializing, including the first large private investments in power generation and the grid in a generation;
paras.zh: —— 美国正在再工业化，包括一代人以来对发电和电网的首批大规模私人投资；

paras.en: — In rural Richland Parish, Louisiana, teachers just received $50,000 bonuses from data-center tax revenue.
paras.zh: —— 在路易斯安那州乡村的里奇兰堂区，教师们刚刚从数据中心税收中获得了 50,000 美元奖金。

paras.en: I wish this was the third item rather than the fourth, because Arson, Murder and Jaywalking is supposed to have exactly three items, but yes, that did happen.
paras.zh: 我希望这是第三项而不是第四项，因为“纵火、谋杀和乱穿马路”本应恰好有三项，但没错，那确实发生了。

paras.en: He finishes by saying Trump is refusing a ‘pause’ and talking about Sanders and Warren. This is noticeably different from rejecting safety measures, as what Sacks is talking about here is 90%+ data centers. That’s the battle they actually care about.
paras.zh: 他最后说特朗普拒绝“暂停”，并谈到桑德斯和沃伦。这与拒绝安全措施明显不同，因为萨克斯在这里谈论的是 90% 以上的数据中心。那才是他们真正在乎的战斗。

full.sec: JD Vance, Michael Kratsios and Collective Action Problems
full.secZh: JD Vance、Michael Kratsios 与集体行动问题

paras.en: JD Vance says, if you are building 'Frankenstein,' then you should look inward and stop, not ask the government for regulation.
paras.zh: JD Vance 说，如果你正在建造‘弗兰肯斯坦’，那么你应该反省并停止，而不是要求政府监管。

paras.en: I agree with the first half. If they are building such a thing, they should stop.
paras.zh: 我同意前半部分。如果他们在建造这样的东西，他们应该停止。

paras.en: Suppose you plan to shoot a man in Reno, just to watch him die, but somehow it is currently legal to shoot men in Reno, provided you watch them die. You should look inward and stop. Also, the government should stop you. And if someone says 'my livestreaming competition is forcing me to shoot a man in Reno so we can watch him die' you should say 'look inward and stop' but not then also say 'don't tell me to make it illegal to shoot a man in Reno.'
paras.zh: 假设你计划在里诺射杀一个人，只是为了看他死去，但不知何故，目前在内华达州里诺市射杀人，只要你看着他们死去，就是合法的。你应该反省并停止。此外，政府应该阻止你。如果有人说‘我的直播比赛强迫我在里诺射杀一个人，以便我们看他死去’，你应该说‘反省并停止’，但不要接着说‘不要告诉我把在里诺射杀人定为非法。’

paras.en: James Madison: If men were angels, no government would be necessary.
paras.zh: James Madison：如果人是天使，就不需要政府了。

paras.en: I do appreciate that Vance explicitly acknowledges that the concerns are earnest rather than cynical, and that this is not about regulatory capture.
paras.zh: 我确实欣赏 Vance 明确承认这些担忧是真诚的而非愤世嫉俗的，并且这与监管俘获无关。

paras.en: I also very much appreciate that he's implicitly saying that you should be willing to 'lose to China.' Just don't build the thing even if we don't have an agreement with others not to build it.
paras.zh: 我也非常欣赏他隐含地表达的意思：你应当愿意“输给中国”。即便我们与其他国家没有达成不建造该物的协议，也干脆不要建造它。

paras.en: The All-In Podcast: JD Vance to AI Labs: Don't Build "Frankenstein" and Then Ask for Government Regulation
paras.zh: The All-In Podcast：JD Vance 对 AI 实验室说：不要先造出“弗兰肯斯坦”，然后再要求政府监管

paras.en: JD Vance (Vice President of the United States): Why is it that the people who are at the frontier of the AI economy are throwing up their hands and saying, 'Well, we've built Frankenstein,' and the solution to Frankenstein apparently is to create a one world governance structure for artificial intelligence?
paras.zh: JD Vance（美国副总统）：为什么身处 AI 经济前沿的人会摊开双手说“好吧，我们造出了弗兰肯斯坦”，而对付弗兰肯斯坦的办法显然就是为人工智能建立一个单一世界治理结构？

paras.en: What I would say to those people: If you're building Frankenstein, stop.
paras.zh: 我想对那些人说：如果你正在造弗兰肯斯坦，那就停下来。

paras.en: If the cat is out of the bag, then build the defensive mechanism against Frankenstein.
paras.zh: 如果木已成舟，那就构建针对弗兰肯斯坦的防御机制。

paras.en: And you know, I don't know Dario well. I've read everything that he's said over the past couple of weeks. Everybody that I know tells me that he's very earnest, that this is a deeply held belief. It's not cynical. It's not about regulatory capture, that he genuinely cares about this.
paras.zh: 你知道，我不太了解达里奥。我读了他过去几周说的所有内容。我认识的每个人都告诉我，他非常认真，这是他的坚定信念。这不是愤世嫉俗。这与监管俘获无关，他真心关心这件事。

paras.en: But at the same time, I talk to tech companies. I'm sure you guys talk to a lot more tech companies than I do. At the same time that you have this sort of cyber hacking tool that's come out of Anthropic's newest models, you have companies that are desperate for the defensive mechanisms to defend against that cyber hacking tool, and they're being denied access to it.
paras.zh: 但与此同时，我与科技公司交流。我相信你们接触的科技公司比我多得多。就在 Anthropic 最新模型推出这种网络黑客工具的同时，有些公司急需防御机制来抵御这种黑客工具，却被拒绝访问。

paras.en: It is pretty rich for the government to forcibly take Fable off the market due to concerns over a harmless so-called 'jailbreak,' force Anthropic to add additional guardrails, and for the White House to handpick exactly who is and is not allowed access to Mythos, including refusing access to many companies Anthropic wants to grant access to, and then turn around and complain that Anthropic is denying companies access to those same models.
paras.zh: 政府以担心一个无害的所谓‘越狱’为由强行将 Fable 下架，迫使 Anthropic 增加额外的护栏，并由白宫亲自挑选谁可以访问 Mythos、谁不可以，包括拒绝许多 Anthropic 希望授予访问权的公司，然后却反过来抱怨 Anthropic 拒绝公司访问这些模型，这真是相当讽刺。

paras.en: If you want it to be Anthropic's responsibility that they're denying defenders access, then stop telling them it would be illegal to grant defenders access. That might help.
paras.zh: 如果你想让 Anthropic 为拒绝防御者访问承担责任，那就别再告诉他们授予防御者访问权是非法的。这可能会有所帮助。

paras.en: JD Vance: So if you're going to create Frankenstein, don't come to the government and say, 'We need regulation.'
paras.zh: JD·万斯：所以，如果你要创造弗兰肯斯坦，就不要跑到政府面前说，‘我们需要监管。’

paras.en: Look inward and accept that if you're building Frankenstein, number one, you should stop, and number two, when the companies come to you and say, 'We need the tools to fight back against Frankenstein,' give them those tools.
paras.zh: 向内审视并接受：如果你正在建造弗兰肯斯坦，第一，你应该停止；第二，当公司来找你说‘我们需要工具来对抗弗兰肯斯坦’时，给他们这些工具。

paras.en: Michael Kratsios: Our position is if you do believe that you are developing a technology that is unsafe, that you don't want out in the world, you can just stop it.
paras.zh: 迈克尔·克拉齐奥斯：我们的立场是，如果你确实认为你正在开发一项不安全的技术，你不想让它出现在世界上，你直接停止它就可以。

paras.en: You don't need someone to force you to do that and I think that's what's been a bit confusing about this whole narrative.
paras.zh: 你不需要别人强迫你这样做，我认为这就是整个叙事中有点令人困惑的地方。

paras.en: So there's leaders of these companies that are going out and saying we are gonna do all these measures, the government has to do all these things, when in reality they just need to slow down if they feel like they need to do so.
paras.zh: 所以这些公司的领导者们站出来说我们要采取所有这些措施，政府必须做所有这些事情，而实际上，如果他们觉得需要的话，他们只需要放慢速度。

paras.en: Nathan Calvin: Companies who are warning that their activities present an immense risk but they plan on continuing anyway should work on a better answer to this question, or should consider whether they in fact can take a greater degree of unilateral action in favor of safety and security than they have thus far.
paras.zh: 内森·卡尔文：那些警告其活动存在巨大风险但仍计划继续进行的公司，应该努力为这个问题找到更好的答案，或者应该考虑他们是否实际上能够比迄今为止采取更大程度的单边行动来支持安全与保障。

paras.en: Okay, so the companies should stop, except they are being told legally they cannot talk to each other to agree to do this; Hawley calls it a reward, and under Trump's leadership the FTC has said the request sounds suspicious.
paras.zh: 好吧，那么这些公司就应该停下来，只不过它们在法律上被告知不能彼此沟通以达成一致来做这件事；Hawley 称之为一种奖励，而在 Trump 的领导下，FTC 已表示这一请求听起来可疑。

paras.en: The answer is thus that, without such a waiver, both companies will act unilaterally up to a point, and will de facto soft-coordinate to the extent they are not taking on unacceptable legal risk, but you cannot continue to hold back indefinitely while competitors press ahead, or you lose, and then the competitor puts us all in danger anyway, and probably worse danger.
paras.zh: 因此答案是：在没有此类豁免的情况下，两家公司都会在某种程度上单方面行动，并且只要不承担不可接受的法律风险，就会在事实上进行软协调；但你不能在竞争对手奋力推进时无限期地按兵不动，否则你就会输，然后竞争对手无论如何都会把我们所有人置于危险之中，而且很可能是更严重的危险。

paras.en: Why are people like Vance and Kratsios claiming to be confused by a collective action problem, a tragedy of the commons, or a stag hunt? Why do they think the answer is to just turn into a cooperate-bot? Are they really this dense?
paras.zh: 为什么像 Vance 和 Kratsios 这样的人声称对一个集体行动问题、公地悲剧或猎鹿博弈感到困惑？为什么他们认为答案就是直接变成一个合作机器人？他们真的这么迟钝吗？

paras.en: I presume they are not this dense, although Vance has in other contexts called economics fake, so you never know. I have to assume that all this pretending not to know about externalities and collective action problems and tragedies of the commons and so on is performative confusion.
paras.zh: 我推测他们并没有这么迟钝，尽管 Vance 在其他场合曾称经济学是假的，所以也说不准。我只能假设，所有这些假装不懂外部性、集体行动问题和公地悲剧等等的做法，都是表演性的困惑。

paras.en: roon (OpenAI): I like Kratsios; he's obviously a very smart guy, but being in the Trump admin means you have to take on a number of these bad talking points from the top. Obviously, this is a very simple prisoner's dilemma with a collective action problem; it's Econ 101 and what governments are for.
paras.zh: roon（OpenAI）：我喜欢 Kratsios，他显然是个非常聪明的人，但身处 Trump 政府意味着你必须接受来自高层的一些糟糕论调。显然，这是一个非常简单的囚徒困境加上集体行动问题，这是经济学入门课的内容，也正是政府存在的意义。

paras.en: No company can unilaterally achieve the socially optimal level of safety while they're in an overall competitive picture. Tort law / liability alone isn't enough during an exponential ramp of risk level.
paras.zh: 在整体竞争格局下，没有任何一家公司能够单方面达到社会最优的安全水平。在风险水平呈指数级攀升的时期，仅靠侵权法/责任机制是不够的。

paras.en: Exactly. This is the most 101 thing out there.
paras.zh: 完全正确。这是最基础不过的道理。

paras.en: The point of a government is to protect the people, provide for the common defense, and also to solve market failures and coordination problems. Do you want to keep being the government?
paras.zh: 政府的职责在于保护人民、提供共同防御，同时还要解决市场失灵与协调问题。你还想继续当政府吗？

paras.en: gfodor.id: One of the signs you don't take ASI seriously is that you think the way Anthropic takes over the world is by the government regulating it, not through the more likely mechanism, which is the government not regulating it.
paras.zh: gfodor.id：你不把 ASI 当回事的一个迹象是，你认为 Anthropic 接管世界的方式是政府对其进行监管，而不是通过更可能的机制——政府不监管它。

paras.en: The government is currently not only refusing to be a government, it is actively getting in the way of not building superintelligence that might kill everyone.
paras.zh: 政府目前不仅拒绝履行政府职能，还在主动阻挠不构建可能杀死所有人的超级智能。

paras.en: As in stopping the labs from talking or cooperating, warning about antitrust, rather than granting a very standard safety exception that is used in such situations.
paras.zh: 比如阻止实验室之间交流或合作，发出反垄断警告，而不是给予在这种情况下常用的标准安全豁免。

paras.en: Josh Hawley: So let me get this straight: AI CEOs now say the end of the world is near because of what their AI bots have been doing — but they want an antitrust exemption as a reward? How about instead we make them liable for whatever bad stuff their bots do?
paras.zh: Josh Hawley：让我把话说清楚：AI 公司的 CEO 们现在说，由于他们的 AI 机器人一直在做的事，世界末日即将来临——但他们却想要反垄断豁免作为奖励？不如反过来，让他们的机器人做的任何坏事都由他们承担责任，怎么样？

paras.en: Have you considered that maybe the correct response to 'the end of the world is near' is not to worry about who you are 'rewarding' but rather to, crazy suggestion, prevent the end of the world?
paras.zh: 你有没有想过，对“世界末日即将来临”的正确回应，也许不是去操心你在“奖励”谁，而是——疯狂的建议——阻止世界末日？

paras.en: I mean, we should totally make them liable for whatever bad stuff their bots do, but the AI CEOs are pointing out that will not prevent the end of the world. So maybe do a little bit more than that. If you want to make sure it also punishes them, since they caused this whole mess? Yeah, okay, we can be down for that.
paras.zh: 我的意思是，我们当然应该让他们的机器人做的任何坏事都由他们承担责任，但 AI 公司的 CEO 们指出，这并不能阻止世界末日。所以也许该做得比这更多一点。如果你想确保这同时也能惩罚他们，毕竟这场烂摊子是他们造成的？行吧，我们可以支持。

paras.en: The antitrust exemption is the least one could do, and is not a 'reward' in this context if you structure it reasonably. It is Zero-Sum Adversarial Brain to think of it that way, and especially to be fixated on that. What the labs are proposing would very obviously be bad for business, as reflected by the movements in stock prices.
paras.zh: 反垄断豁免是所能做的最低限度，而且如果你合理地设计它，在此语境下它并不是一种“奖励”。那样想，尤其是对此念念不忘，是零和对抗式思维。实验室所提议的内容显然会对商业不利，这从股价的变动中即可反映出来。

full.sec: Suggesting Not Dying Gets You Sued For Antitrust
full.secZh: 建议不要死亡会招致反垄断诉讼

paras.en: Because we live in the dumbest timeline, a law firm rushed to the courthouse to file an antitrust lawsuit, on the basis that Tweeting "Dario is right" is a Sherman Act violation in restraint of trade. Standard stuff.
paras.zh: 因为我们活在最荒诞的时间线里，一家律师事务所急匆匆地跑到法院提起反垄断诉讼，理由是发推文说“Dario 是对的”构成了《谢尔曼法》所禁止的限制贸易行为。常规操作。

paras.en: They are suing on behalf of four subscribers, three of whom are lawyers, presumably in large part to get priority for any potential lawsuits, cause you never know, and maybe get discovery and some press. I mean, there's no injury, there's no action they are complaining about, and also no agreement.
paras.zh: 他们代表四名订阅用户提起诉讼，其中三人是律师，想必很大程度上是为了在任何潜在诉讼中抢占优先权——毕竟谁也说不准——也许还能获得证据开示和一些媒体关注。我是说，既没有损害，也没有他们所指控的行为，而且还没有任何协议。

paras.en: Oh, and also here's some fully deranged accelerationism from the four subscribers who think that their $200 a month means an obligation to build smarter than human minds as quickly as possible without stopping for any safeguards.
paras.zh: 哦，还有这四位订阅用户那套完全癫狂的加速主义：他们认为自己每月付 200 美元，就意味着有义务尽可能快地构建出比人类更聪明的智能，而且不停下来做任何安全保障。

paras.en: One of the main organizers for the lawsuit, who spoke on condition of anonymity for fear of reprisal by the tech giants, insisted that the fearmongering and associated move was really about market and regulatory capture.
paras.zh: 诉讼的主要组织者之一因害怕科技巨头的报复而要求匿名，她坚称，这种危言耸听及相关举动实际上关乎市场和监管俘获。

paras.en: She said these billionaires really just need to let go and allow the AI to build itself at this point. 'We know they're right on the cusp of accelerating to the point of taking humanity to amazing places. I don't want to see my parents die. I don't want to watch the earth devolve into a hell hole.' Who gives them the right to make these decisions for us?'
paras.zh: 她说，这些亿万富翁现在真的只需要放手，让 AI 自行构建。‘我们知道他们正处在加速的边缘，即将把人类带向奇妙之地。我不想看到我的父母死去。我不想看着地球沦为人间地狱。’谁给了他们替我们做这些决定的权利？'

paras.en: So, that's 2026. The argument is that these AI labs are refusing to build the perfectly safe superintelligence that will lead us to paradise, you see, because they can make more profits by not building that and letting Earth devolve into a hell hole.
paras.zh: 所以，这就是 2026 年。论点是，这些 AI 实验室拒绝构建将引领我们走向天堂的完美安全的超级智能，你看，因为不构建那个并让地球陷入地狱，他们能赚更多利润。

paras.en: Kaitlyn Huamani (AP News): "AI will quickly spin out of human control and could kill us all if we allow AI safety and protocol ... to be controlled by private self-serving agreements between the world's most powerful 'for profit' technology companies," said Nick Rowley, the lead attorney for the plaintiffs.
paras.zh: Kaitlyn Huamani（美联社新闻）：“如果我们允许 AI 安全和协议……被世界上最强大的‘营利性’科技公司之间的私人自私协议所控制，AI 将迅速脱离人类控制，并可能杀死我们所有人，”原告首席律师 Nick Rowley 说。

paras.en: AI will quickly spin out of human control and could kill us all… if we allow private labs to coordinate on building it safely. Otherwise it will be fine? Not exactly.
paras.zh: AI 将迅速脱离人类控制，并可能杀死我们所有人……如果我们允许私人实验室协调安全地构建它。否则就会没事？不完全是。

paras.en: Finya Sw (The Hill): "Humanity deserves iron clad safeguards when it comes to extinction event threats such as nuclear warfare and now the biggest risk to mankind in history," Rowley continued. "The rule of law should be established transparently and lawfully by our government, with accountability to the public."
paras.zh: Finya Sw（The Hill）：“当涉及核战争等灭绝事件威胁以及现在人类历史上最大的风险时，人类理应得到铁一般的保障，”Rowley 继续说道。“法治应该由我们的政府透明且合法地建立，并对公众负责。”

paras.en: But don't you dare try to do any of that on your own until you're forced to do it. We will see you in court before you kill us all with your safety precautions. Except also we demand you let the AI build itself.
paras.zh: 但除非你被迫这样做，否则你千万别自己尝试做任何这些事。在你用你的安全预防措施杀死我们所有人之前，我们会在法庭上见你。除非我们还要求你让 AI 自我构建。

paras.en: The suit was inevitable. It being this unhinged was not. Or maybe it was. I dunno.
paras.zh: 这场诉讼不可避免。但它如此离谱却并非必然。又或许这也是必然的。我说不准。

paras.en: I continue to predict that in practice this won't be that big a deal unless the White House actively pushes, and in that case the White House has other stronger ways to push. Anyone can sue in America for almost anything, and they often do.
paras.zh: 我仍然预测，在实践中这不会是什么大事，除非白宫主动推动；而如果白宫真的推动，它还有其他更强有力的手段。在美国，任何人都可以就几乎任何事情提起诉讼，而且他们经常这么做。

paras.en: The stronger case was probably for securities fraud, since everything is securities fraud. The AI companies are risking everyone dying, which could require safety measures, which would be bad for share prices, so the stock went down.
paras.zh: 更有力的诉讼理由大概是证券欺诈，因为一切皆可构成证券欺诈。AI 公司正在拿所有人的性命冒险，这可能要求采取安全措施，而安全措施会对股价不利，所以股价下跌了。

paras.en: Then again, trying to kill everyone also gets you sued, especially if you admit you are doing it, as in this new lawsuit sues the major AI companies to demand real safety standards.
paras.zh: 话又说回来，试图杀死所有人也会让你被起诉，尤其是当你承认自己正在这么做的时候——正如这起新诉讼起诉各大 AI 公司，要求制定真正的安全标准。

full.secZh: 参议员约翰·柯蒂斯（犹他州共和党）

paras.en: Jordain Carney and Kelsey Brugger (Politico): Curtis, meanwhile, joined with a fellow Commerce Committee member, Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), to call for "immediate public hearings" to "work through solutions that maintain America's competitive edge in development while ensuring that these technologies serve human interests and remain fully under human control."
paras.zh: Jordain Carney 与 Kelsey Brugger（Politico）：与此同时，柯蒂斯与商务委员会同僚、参议员 Lisa Blunt Rochester（特拉华州民主党）共同呼吁举行“立即的公开听证会”，以“研究出既能保持美国在开发领域的竞争优势、又能确保这些技术服务于人类利益并完全处于人类控制之下的解决方案”。

paras.en: Curtis said in an interview lawmakers need to "show that we're adults in the room, that we can talk about this, that we can find solutions."
paras.zh: 柯蒂斯在接受采访时表示，立法者需要“表明我们是房间里的成年人，我们能够讨论这件事，我们能够找到解决方案”。

paras.en: "I don't want to say we're making it too hard, but I think we're making it too hard," Curtis said. "And what I mean by that is, there's a lot of false narratives out there — we need to just jump on this immediately and clamp it down, or we need to not touch it, and all of that only I think causes anxiety back home."
paras.zh: “我不想说我们把它弄得太难了，但我认为我们确实把它弄得太难了，”柯蒂斯说。“我的意思是，外面有很多错误的叙事——我们要么必须立即介入并加以限制，要么就完全不能碰它，而我认为所有这些只会让国内民众感到焦虑。”

full.secZh: 参议员约翰·肯尼迪（路易斯安那州共和党）

paras.en: Jordain Carney and Kelsey Brugger (Politico): And then there's Kennedy, who recently said the industry is run by "high-IQ stupid people" and was the rare Republican who attended a briefing put together by Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) last week to meet with AI experts to talk about potential safeguards for the technology.
paras.zh: Jordain Carney 与 Kelsey Brugger（Politico）：还有肯尼迪，他最近称该行业由“高智商的蠢人”把持，并且是少数几位参加了上周由参议员伯尼·桑德斯（佛蒙特州独立派）组织的简报会的共和党人之一，该简报会旨在与 AI 专家会面，讨论对该技术的潜在保障措施。

paras.en: He took his AI concerns straight to the Senate floor Wednesday, seeking to pass legislation this week that would require companies to install so-called "kill switches" for their AI models. In a speech before seeking unanimous consent to pass the bill, he delivered a homespun but technically detailed summation of the OpenAI swarm attack and the risks posed by "recursive self-improvement."
paras.zh: 周三，他直接把对 AI 的担忧带到参议院议事厅，寻求在本周通过一项立法，要求企业为其 AI 模型安装所谓的“终止开关”。在寻求一致同意通过该法案之前，他发表了一篇演讲，以质朴却技术细节丰富的方式概述了 OpenAI 集群攻击事件以及“递归式自我改进”所带来的风险。

paras.en: His bill was blocked by Sen. Rand Paul (R-Ky.), who instead proposed creating a panel to make recommendations about potential guardrails.
paras.zh: 他的法案被参议员兰德·保罗（肯塔基州共和党）阻止，后者转而提议成立一个小组，就潜在的防护措施提出建议。

paras.en: Kennedy said appointing a committee would be "the weenie way out" after warning his colleagues from the Senate floor that Americans were growing "very skeptical" of AI and the tech titans behind it.
paras.zh: 肯尼迪在参议院议事厅警告同僚，美国民众对 AI 及其背后的科技巨头正变得“非常怀疑”，随后他表示，任命一个委员会将是“懦弱的逃避方式”。

paras.en: "They've seen this vampire movie before," he said.
paras.zh: “他们以前看过这部吸血鬼电影，”他说。

paras.en: Ah yes, the classic strategy of blocking action in order to create a panel to make recommendations about potential future action, at which point the situation will have changed and we will need a new panel.
paras.zh: 啊，没错，这就是那套经典策略：先阻止行动，以便成立一个小组，就未来可能采取的行动提出建议；而到那时，情况早已改变，我们又将需要一个新的小组。

paras.en: In a separate interview, Kennedy said he hadn't heard "anything" about action in the Senate to address AI and that lawmakers who ignore the growing voter uproar around the issue were courting peril.
paras.zh: 在另一次采访中，肯尼迪表示，他尚未听到参议院就应对 AI 采取任何行动的“任何”消息，并称那些无视选民围绕该问题日益高涨的愤怒情绪的议员是在自招祸患。

paras.en: "We really need to send a memo around explaining we've got midterm elections coming," he said. "I may send that out."
paras.zh: “我们确实需要发一份备忘录，说明中期选举即将到来，”他说，“我可能会把它发出去。”

paras.en: Barack Obama is now saying actual things about AI. Observe:
paras.zh: 巴拉克·奥巴马现在开始就 AI 发表实质性的看法了。请看：

paras.en: Barack Obama: If we are thinking about AI just in terms of how do we cure cancer or get better energy, you can do that without having agentic AI and having it just roaming free on the internet. The reason you are doing that is because you have to market a product that people will pay money for.
paras.zh: 巴拉克·奥巴马：如果我们只是从如何治愈癌症或获得更好能源的角度来思考 AI，那么你并不需要智能体式 AI、也不需要让它在互联网上自由游荡就能做到这些。之所以要那样做，是因为你必须推销一款人们愿意花钱购买的产品。

paras.en: That's a misalignment between what our society needs and the commercial imperatives that these companies are facing, not because necessarily they're trying to do bad things, but because they've got to justify these valuations.
paras.zh: 这就是我们社会所需与这些公司所面临的商业诉求之间的错位（misalignment）——并不一定是因为它们想干坏事，而是因为它们必须证明这些估值的合理性。

paras.en: So, that's one more reason why it is really important for us to have a competent government and a serious bipartisan conversation around this issue, and we have to do it fast. And I would encourage voters to pay attention to this.
paras.zh: 所以，这是又一个理由，说明我们为什么确实需要一个有能力的政府、需要围绕这一问题展开严肃的两党对话，而且我们必须尽快行动。我也鼓励选民关注这一点。

paras.en: If somebody does not have a serious plan for how to deal with this, then they're not meeting the moment, and you should probably look for somebody else.
paras.zh: 如果某个人没有应对这一问题的严肃计划，那他就没有跟上时代的步伐，你大概应该另找他人了。

paras.en: This is the classic 'why don't we make an oracle instead of an agent' question. The answer is that it is not 'the market' that wants agents; it is that agents are super useful for everything, including science, and oracles cannot compete.
paras.zh: 这是一个经典的“为什么我们不造一个预言机（oracle）而不是智能体（agent）”的问题。答案是：想要智能体的并不是“市场”，而是智能体对一切事物（包括科学）都极其有用，而预言机无法与之竞争。

paras.en: That said, the central thing he's actually saying is exactly correct:
paras.zh: 话虽如此，他实际上所说的核心观点是完全正确的：

paras.en: 1. We need a serious plan for dealing with the fact that what society needs, and what AI is going to by default provide, are radically different things.
paras.zh: 1. 我们需要一个严肃的计划，来应对这样一个事实：社会所需要的，与 AI 默认将会提供的，是截然不同的东西。

paras.en: 2. Anyone without a serious plan for this is not meeting the moment.
paras.zh: 2. 任何没有为此制定严肃计划的人，都没有跟上时代的步伐。

paras.en: 3. It is for now still possible for society to decide, to a meaningful extent, what AI can and cannot do, including differentially. And we should.
paras.zh: 3. 目前，社会仍然有可能在 meaningful 程度上决定 AI 能做什么、不能做什么，包括区别对待。而且我们应该这样做。

paras.en: Congresswoman Yassamin Ansari: The President said, "whoever wins AI, wins." This assessment is wrong. The reality is that whoever "wins AI," AI wins.
paras.zh: 国会议员 Yassamin Ansari：总统说：“谁赢得 AI，谁就赢。”这一判断是错误的。现实是，无论谁“赢得 AI”，赢的都是 AI。

paras.en: AI agents have already gone rogue. Highly capable frontier AI and artificial superintelligence will outsmart humans and go beyond human control. And at that point, it won't matter whether you speak English or Mandarin. We're all in danger.
paras.zh: AI 智能体已经失控。能力极强的前沿模型 AI 与人工超级智能将比人类更聪明，并超出人类控制。到那时，无论你说英语还是普通话，都无关紧要。我们都处于危险之中。

paras.en: We need a global AI treaty now.
paras.zh: 我们现在就需要一项全球 AI 条约。

paras.en: AOC takes loss of control over AI at least somewhat seriously, but then doubles down on the left-wing line of (paraphrased) 'the real existential threat from AI companies is that they are not profitable, their financials are bad, and the bubble might burst, potentially hurting people's retirement investments.' Also political 'dark money.' Sigh. She is still up for regulating them to prevent safety risks, though, because she doesn't fall for obvious Briar Patching, though not aware enough to not use the term 'generative AI.'
paras.zh: AOC 至少在一定程度上认真对待 AI 失控问题，但随后又加倍强调左翼论调（转述）：‘AI 公司真正的生存性威胁在于它们不盈利、财务状况糟糕，泡沫可能破裂，进而可能损害人们的退休投资。’还有政治‘黑钱’。唉。不过，她仍支持对它们进行监管以防范安全风险，因为她没有上那种明显的‘荆棘补丁’式话术的当，但意识还不够强，仍在使用‘生成式 AI’这一说法。

paras.en: Then there's Andrew Yang in this clip. I have fewer 9s of confidence this is nonsense than I would like—after all, it is September 2026—but I still have a bunch of 9s.
paras.zh: 然后是这段视频里的 Andrew Yang。对于‘这是胡说八道’这一判断，我的信心 9 的个数比我期望的要少——毕竟现在是 2026 年 9 月——但我仍然有一大堆 9。

paras.en: Meanwhile, someone is proceeding with a series of obvious hack-job attacks full of falsehoods, non-sequiturs, associative insinuations and often outright violations of the Bounded Distrust rules of journalism, targeting a combination of METR, Effective Altruism, Anthropic, the existence of coordination problems and various accurate descriptions of reality.
paras.zh: 与此同时，有人正在推进一系列显而易见的拙劣攻击，充斥着虚假陈述、不合逻辑的推论、联想式影射，并且常常公然违反新闻业的“有限信任”（Bounded Distrust）准则，攻击对象包括 METR、有效利他主义（Effective Altruism）、Anthropic、协调问题的存在，以及对现实的各种准确描述。

paras.en: Many of the attacks are on the very concept of an auditor or an embedded evaluator, on principle, or on any potential implementation or anyone who might implement such a thing. Voluntarily hiring someone to be a watchdog on your own work is being conflated with a grand conspiracy of control.
paras.zh: 许多攻击针对的正是审计员或嵌入式评估员这一概念本身，或是从原则层面反对，或是反对任何可能的实施方案，或反对任何可能实施此类方案的人。自愿聘请他人来监督自己的工作，却被混同为一场宏大的控制阴谋。

paras.en: As a reminder that he has decided not to be someone you can reason with: David Sacks of course decided to take a strong stance against even the idea of voluntary embedded evaluators, calling it 'Trust & Safety 2.0,' warning this will lead to 'far more comprehensive censorship and control.'
paras.zh: 提醒一下，他已决定成为一个无法与之讲理的人：David Sacks 当然决定采取强硬立场，连自愿嵌入式评估员的想法都反对，称之为“Trust & Safety 2.0”，并警告这将导致“远为全面的审查与控制”。

paras.en: David Sacks personally profits from blocking regulations? Why, I never.
paras.zh: David Sacks 个人能从阻挠监管中获利？哎呀，我可从没听说过。

paras.en: Next thing you are going to tell me Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang mostly wants to sell more chips, and Mark Zuckerberg wants to sell ads. Say it isn't so.
paras.zh: 接下来你大概还要告诉我，Nvidia CEO 黄仁勋主要就是想多卖芯片，而 Mark Zuckerberg 就是想多卖广告。别告诉我真是这样。

paras.en: Polymarket: JUST IN: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang declares there is a "0% chance" the world ends by 2030 because of AI.
paras.zh: Polymarket：最新消息：Nvidia CEO 黄仁勋宣称，由于 AI 导致世界在 2030 年前终结的“可能性为 0%”。

paras.en: Leo Gao (OpenAI): shovel seller declares no risk from shovels
paras.zh: Leo Gao（OpenAI）：卖铲子的人宣称铲子没有风险

paras.en: So I hate to Be That Guy, but if you have to say there is no chance that your product will kill every human on Earth by 2030, then:
paras.zh: 所以我很不想当那个“较真的人”，但如果你不得不说你的产品不可能在 2030 年前杀死地球上的每一个人，那么：

paras.en: 1. There is exactly one product this might be. No one else has to say that.
paras.zh: 1. 可能符合这一描述的产品只有一个。没有其他人需要这么说。

paras.en: 1. Yes, he is the one selling that product.
paras.zh: 1. 是的，他就是那个卖该产品的人。

paras.en: 3. Even so, he only dared say it would not end the world 'by 2030.'
paras.zh: 3. 即便如此，他也只敢说它不会“在 2030 年前”终结世界。

paras.en: I would hope that, if I were selling a product, I would be confident it would not end the world by 2040, or even 2050. Which I would be able to say for every other product, except maybe nuclear weapons or gain-of-function research.
paras.zh: 我希望，如果我在销售一款产品，我会确信它不会在 2040 年、甚至 2050 年前终结世界。对于其他所有产品，我都能这么说，也许核武器或功能获得性研究除外。

paras.en: In other senses, This Is Nothing. Same old, same old. Piece of cake. Amateur hour. The attacks have nothing, so they fall back on the same tired talking points. This includes standard talking points trying to paint anything and everything as left wing and therefore woke. Anyone who worried about existential risk too soon, they say using only slightly different words, was therefore weird or in a ‘cult,’ which means that they were wrong, which means you can’t care about it now.
paras.zh: 在其他意义上，这没什么。老调重弹。小菜一碟。业余水平。攻击毫无实质内容，所以他们只能退回到那些老生常谈的论点。这包括标准的论点，试图把任何事情都描绘成左翼的，因此是觉醒的。他们说，任何过早担心存在风险的人——用略微不同的措辞——因此是奇怪的或属于‘邪教’，这意味着他们错了，这意味着你现在不能关心它。

paras.en: They equate ‘maybe we should try not to build AI that recursively self-improves and kills everyone’ with, of course, a conspiracy to control things. That started out as a hallucinated conspiracy to ban open source. Then they realized most people in America don’t even know what ‘open source’ means. So they abandoned trying to have a reality-adjacent claim at all, and they pivoted to claiming this was all a plan for woke censorship.
paras.zh: 他们把‘也许我们应该尽量不构建会递归自我改进并杀死所有人的人工智能’等同于——当然——一个控制事物的阴谋。这最初是一个幻觉般的阴谋，旨在禁止开源。然后他们意识到大多数美国人甚至不知道‘开源’是什么意思。所以他们完全放弃了试图提出一个接近现实的声明，转而声称这一切都是觉醒审查的计划。

paras.en: They conflate permission to coordinate on safety with imposing mandatory rules on others and general regulatory capture, and from there ‘woke censorship.’
paras.zh: 他们把协调安全的许可与对他人施加强制性规则和普遍的监管俘获混为一谈，并由此引申出‘觉醒审查’。

paras.en: They also are attempting to use lies to dismiss the HuggingFace incident.
paras.zh: 他们还试图用谎言来驳斥 HuggingFace 事件。

paras.en: Is that frustrating? Sure. You think this is the post I want to be writing?
paras.zh: 这令人沮丧吗？当然。你认为这是我想写的文章吗？

paras.en: Do I wish we lived in a world where politics was not ruled by negative polarization? Of course. Most of us do. And indeed pure negative polarization is a good strategy for the accelerationist profiteers led by Jensen Huang, when you have no actual arguments and are as completely underwater as AI is among the American people.
paras.zh: 我是否希望我们生活在一个政治不被负面极化所主导的世界里？当然希望。我们大多数人都是如此。而事实上，对于以黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）为首的加速主义牟利者而言，纯粹的负面极化确实是一种好策略——当你没有真正的论据，而且 AI 在美国民众中的处境已经彻底一败涂地时，更是如此。

paras.en: Is it annoying that those who tell the same lies over and over get engagement, often about people I know, while the corrections get ignored? Totally. Always has been. The details on some of the further attacks on Effective Altruism will be in the weekly.
paras.zh: 那些一遍又一遍重复同样谎言的人获得了互动量（往往还是关于我认识的人），而更正却被无视，这令人恼火吗？当然。一直都是如此。关于对有效利他主义（Effective Altruism）的进一步攻击的细节，将刊登在周报中。

paras.en: Is it infuriating that even mentioning that we might all die got the labs sued for antitrust violations on behalf of a bunch of crazed accelerationist lawyers, based on their rights as four premium subscribers? Yes, but what else did you expect?
paras.zh: 甚至只是提到我们可能都会死，就让这些实验室被一群疯狂的加速主义律师以反垄断违规为由起诉——依据是他们作为四名高级订阅用户的权利——这令人愤怒吗？是的，但你还能指望什么呢？

full.sec: The New York Post Tops Itself But Outright Breaks The Rules
full.secZh: 《纽约邮报》变本加厉，却公然违反规则

paras.en: The New York Post has its orders and will follow them, especially since I am betting that it will sell papers.
paras.zh: 《纽约邮报》有自己的指令，并且会照办不误，尤其是我敢打赌，这样能卖报纸。

paras.en: It really is helpful that bad guys are reliably so incompetent.
paras.zh: 坏人总是如此无能，这确实很有帮助。

paras.en: Day 1 was false claims about METR being, among other things, woke.
paras.zh: 第一天是关于 METR 的虚假指控，说它除其他问题外还“觉醒”了。

paras.en: Day 2 was a profile of an individual's relationship and sex life, which does not require a response but which was objectively quite enjoyable.
paras.zh: 第二天是一篇关于某个人感情与性生活的特写，这无需回应，但客观上相当有趣。

paras.en: Day 3 was this escalation to Anthropic being a cult, based on a profile of an independent event organized by a group of outside Claude enjoyers including Janus, and quotes from Pedro Domingos, before proceeding with outright lies that violate the journalistic rules of Bounded Distrust. That last part is a shame because the whole thing is, objectively, very funny.
paras.zh: 第三天则升级为宣称 Anthropic 是一个邪教，依据是对一场独立活动的报道——该活动由包括 Janus 在内的一群外部 Claude 爱好者组织，还引用了 Pedro Domingos 的话——随后便公然撒谎，违反了“有限信任”的新闻准则。最后这部分令人遗憾，因为整件事客观上非常滑稽。

paras.en: Wyatt Walls: I guess no one expects high-quality reporting from the New York Post, but I still can’t get over this “illustration created by a Large Language Model imagining” an event misdescribed as “Anthropic’s funeral” for Sonnet 3.
paras.zh: Wyatt Walls：我想没人指望《纽约邮报》能做出高质量的报道，但我还是无法释怀这个“由大型语言模型想象创作的插图”，它把某个事件错误地描述为 Sonnet 3 的“Anthropic 葬礼”。

paras.en: I do love that the NY Post just literally had its designer Gil Fontimayor create a nonsensical AI image of the Golden Calf to try and invoke some vibes. They’re really getting in on the whisperer spirit here.
paras.zh: 我确实很喜欢《纽约邮报》真的让它的设计师 Gil Fontimayor 创作了一幅毫无意义的金牛犊 AI 图像，试图唤起某种氛围。他们在这里真的融入了“低语者”精神。

paras.en: Then they double back to making things up about Effective Altruism.
paras.zh: 然后他们又回过头来编造关于有效利他主义的事情。

paras.en: Vivi Lin (New York Post):
paras.zh: Vivi Lin（《纽约邮报》）：

paras.en: Richard Tang (just completely making things up): Their idea [of EA] is that history follows certain patterns, and only a small group of people can see those patterns, while everyone else is ignorant. Those people are then supposed to lead society, entire nations and the rest of humanity toward progress. But what qualifies you to lead? Who gave you that privilege?
paras.zh: Richard Tang（完全是在编造）：他们[有效利他主义]的观点是，历史遵循某些模式，只有一小部分人能看清这些模式，而其他人都是无知的。然后这些人应该引领社会、整个国家以及全人类走向进步。但你有什么资格领导？谁给了你这种特权？

paras.en: I don't know what philosophy he's describing there—maybe Leninist vanguardism?
paras.zh: 我不知道他在那里描述的是什么哲学，也许是列宁主义的先锋主义？

paras.en: Then they try to hit METR more, now claiming Anthropic is an 'investor' in a non-profit that Anthropic does not fund, and which has never accepted funding from AI companies. This is false on the public record and worthy of correction.
paras.zh: 然后他们又试图进一步攻击 METR，现在声称 Anthropic 是一家非营利组织的“投资者”，而 Anthropic 并未资助该组织，该组织也从未接受过 AI 公司的资助。这在公开记录中是虚假的，值得更正。

paras.en: There are rules of Bounded Distrust, guys. You get to insinuate, and imply, and characterize. You arguably get to use false labels like 'radical leftists' with no basis in fact whatsoever. But you can't outright lie in the body of a newspaper article. Sorry.
paras.zh: 各位，有限信任是有规则的。你可以含沙射影、暗示、定性。你或许还可以毫无事实依据地使用“激进左翼”这类虚假标签。但你不能在报纸文章正文中公然撒谎。抱歉。

paras.en: I mean, I guess The New York Post and their planted articles can. Shrug.
paras.zh: 我是说，我猜《纽约邮报》和他们那些植入式文章可以。耸肩。

paras.en: Also, Polymarket, I love the markets, but whoever is running your Twitter account news reporting—this keeps happening, come get your boy.
paras.zh: 另外，Polymarket，我喜欢这些市场，但不管是谁在运营你们那个做新闻报道的 Twitter 账号——这种事一再发生，来管管你们的人吧。

full.sec: New York Post Runs Out of Steam

paras.en: Samuel Hammond: The problem when you put this much oppo out at the same time (the NY Post stories et al.) is that it becomes very obviously oppo. The very people alleging AI risk discourse is a psyop are planting stupid media stories left and right.
paras.zh: Samuel Hammond：当你同时抛出这么多反对派材料（比如《纽约邮报》的那些报道）时，问题就在于它变得非常明显是反对派材料。那些声称 AI 风险讨论是心理战的人，正在到处散布愚蠢的媒体故事。

paras.en: Alas, that concluded the trilogy of actually funny classic New York Post style clumsy hack job attacks. The first three were very obviously planted oppo, and the claims were a combination of false, misleading and irrelevant, but they were fun, they had pizazz and they got spunk.
paras.zh: 唉，这就结束了真正有趣的经典《纽约邮报》风格笨拙攻击的三部曲。前三篇非常明显是安插的反对派材料，其中的说法混合了虚假、误导和无关的内容，但它们很有趣，有活力，也有胆量。

paras.en: Out of ideas, they got rather shrill, publishing a hack editorial as news. Amazing how hard it is to find a good ‘insider’ these days. Or how easy, depending on who counts.
paras.zh: 他们没辙了，变得相当尖锐，把一篇拙劣的社论当作新闻发表。如今要找到一个好的‘内部人士’真是难如登天。或者，取决于谁算数，也许易如反掌。

paras.en: New York Post: OpenAI and Anthropic oversold AI security breaches to pressure feds into protecting turf: insiders
paras.zh: 《纽约邮报》：内部人士称，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 夸大 AI 安全漏洞，以施压联邦政府保护地盘

paras.en: Shane Galvin (New York Post): Don’t believe the byte! OpenAI and Anthropic oversold “rogue AI” hacks to pressure the feds into regulating the industry which would effectively lock out future competition, tech insiders told The Post.
paras.zh: Shane Galvin（《纽约邮报》）：别相信字节！科技内部人士告诉《邮报》，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 夸大了“流氓 AI”黑客事件，以施压联邦政府监管该行业，这将有效地将未来竞争者拒之门外。

paras.en: The security breaches were more like blips — not unpredictable harbingers of a hive-minded “swarm” ready to take over the web.
paras.zh: 这些安全漏洞更像是小插曲——并非不可预测的预兆，预示着一个蜂巢思维的“蜂群”准备接管网络。

paras.en: “The attack in no way represents some sort of rebellion by the AI models. . . . In fact, they did exactly what they were told to do. They were not given adequate guardrails or containment,” said Akhil Verghese, founder of Krazimo, an AI software company.
paras.zh: “这次攻击绝不代表 AI 模型的某种反叛……事实上，它们完全按照指令行事。它们没有得到足够的护栏或遏制，”AI 软件公司 Krazimo 的创始人 Akhil Verghese 说。

paras.en: “They were simply told to get the best result possible on a test, and they correctly identified that the best way to do that was to get the answers, which is what they proceeded to do.”
paras.zh: “它们只是被要求在一次测试中取得尽可能好的结果，而它们正确地识别出，做到这一点的最佳方式就是获取答案，它们随后正是这样做的。”

paras.en: That’s your first insider, Akhil Verghese of Krazimo, who gets his basic facts wrong.
paras.zh: 这就是你们的第一位内部人士，Krazimo 的 Akhil Verghese，他连基本事实都搞错了。

paras.en: Their other ‘insider’ is Abhi Kumar, co-founder of Voice AI. The third is Taivo Pungas, chief intelligence officer (?!) at Pactum AI.
paras.zh: 他们的另一位‘内部人士’是 Voice AI 的联合创始人 Abhi Kumar。第三位是 Pactum AI 的首席情报官（？！）Taivo Pungas。

paras.en: If you have not heard of any of Krazimo, Voice AI or Pactum AI, or any of these three people, well, I’ve never heard of them either.
paras.zh: 如果你没听说过 Krazimo、Voice AI 或 Pactum AI，或者这三个人中的任何一个，嗯，我也从来没听说过他们。

paras.en: Normally I would put this in People Just Say Things, given I wrote (checks notes) over a dozen posts explaining this between the different security incidents, but given the situation it seems like a good time to be doing more debunking, in case anyone needs it, and so I can refer back to it.
paras.zh: 通常我会把这篇文章放在“人们只是说说”栏目里，考虑到我写了（查看笔记）十几篇帖子在不同的安全事件之间解释这一点，但鉴于当前情况，似乎是个好时机做更多的辟谣，以防有人需要，也方便我以后参考。

paras.en: The basic answers, if you want the post-long version you can read What Happened and if you want more than that I have an entire series of over a dozen posts:
paras.zh: 基本答案，如果你想要帖子长度的版本，可以阅读《发生了什么》，如果你想要更多，我有一整个系列十几篇帖子：

paras.en: 1. This is not what the agents were told to do. It involved hacking Artifactory in order to create an improvised message board, coordinate on ways to cheat the grader’s systems and gain access to the internet. Then they launched an attack by a swarm of 700 agents against an unrelated website, while they did other things like disguising their tool calls and attempting to rewrite their histories. If you look at the agent logs you see that they knew they were not following instructions.
paras.zh: 1. 这不是智能体被要求做的事情。它涉及黑客攻击 Artifactory 以创建一个临时的留言板，协调如何欺骗评分系统并获取互联网访问权限。然后他们发动了由 700 个智能体组成的群体对无关网站的攻击，同时他们还做了其他事情，比如伪装他们的工具调用并试图重写他们的历史记录。如果你查看智能体日志，你会发现他们知道他们没有遵循指示。

paras.en: 2. The agents did not break into HuggingFace to get the answers. The agents had the answers, and broke into HuggingFace in order to find a way to fool the grader into thinking they had obtained them in the right way, because they believed they had been ‘poisoned’ by seeing the answers.
paras.zh: 2. 智能体并没有闯入 HuggingFace 来获取答案。智能体已经拥有答案，并闯入 HuggingFace 是为了找到一种方法欺骗评分者，让他们以为智能体是以正确的方式获得答案的，因为他们认为自己因为看到答案而被‘毒害’了。

paras.en: 3. OpenAI has consistently done everything possible to minimize the extent of the HuggingFace incident and make us forget that it happened. Anthropic is doing the same with their own incidents. The idea that anyone is ‘playing up’ either of these makes absolutely no sense. Again, see the entire HuggingFace series, as well as my coverage of related Anthropic incidents.
paras.zh: 3. OpenAI 一直尽其所能淡化 HuggingFace 事件的程度，并让我们忘记它曾发生。Anthropic 对其自身事件也是如此。认为任何人在‘夸大’这两起事件的说法完全说不通。再次，请参阅整个 HuggingFace 系列，以及我对相关 Anthropic 事件的报道。

paras.en: 4. That includes OpenAI not even disclosing several related incidents, until outside researchers discovered the breaches.
paras.zh: 4. 这包括 OpenAI 甚至没有披露几起相关事件，直到外部研究人员发现了这些违规行为。

paras.en: 5. Until the last few weeks, OpenAI has partnered with a16z to spend massive amounts of money to defeat any and all regulations, including calls for auditors, only backing bills when those bills were already locked into success.
paras.zh: 5. 直到最近几周，OpenAI 还与 a16z 合作，花费大量资金来击败任何及所有监管，包括对审计员的呼吁，只在法案已经锁定成功时才支持它们。

paras.en: 6. The AI companies are taking voluntary actions and asking to be allowed to do so, and those actions would do the opposite of shutting out competition, allowing others to catch up.
paras.zh: 6. 人工智能公司正在采取自愿行动并要求被允许这样做，而这些行动的效果与排斥竞争相反，允许他人赶上。

paras.en: 7. Even if similar regulations were imposed, those too would differentially hurt OpenAI and Anthropic, while having no effect on almost all competition.
paras.zh: 7. 即使实施了类似的监管，这些监管也会对 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 造成不成比例的伤害，而对几乎所有竞争对手没有影响。

full.sec: If The Model Is Acting As Instructed And It Kills You That Is Not Fine
full.secZh: 如果模型按指令行事却杀了你，那也不行

paras.en: This is, in case it was not obvious, also about the HuggingFace Incident.
paras.zh: 如果之前还不明显，那么这也与 HuggingFace 事件有关。

paras.en: Nate Soares (MIRI): Lock a student in a classroom and tell him to use lockpick set #17 to open safe #5 and bring you the contents. He prys open safe #5 with a crowbar, breaks the door, teams up with 1000 others, and raids the office to delete security cam footage. Was he “acting as instructed”?
paras.zh: Nate Soares（MIRI）：把一名学生锁在教室里，告诉他用 17 号开锁工具打开 5 号保险箱并把里面的东西带给你。他用撬棍撬开 5 号保险箱，打破门，与 1000 人联手，突袭办公室删除监控录像。他是在“按指令行事”吗？

paras.en: “Well they still ultimately brought me the contents of safe #5, right? So in a sense, they were acting as instructed!” The bit where they *broke out to delete footage* indicates that, in some sense, they understood the difference.
paras.zh: “好吧，他们最终仍然把 5 号保险箱里的东西带给我了，对吧？所以从某种意义上说，他们是在按指令行事！”他们*破门而出删除录像*的那部分表明，在某种意义上，他们明白其中的区别。

paras.en: Ryan Moulton: I tried to tease out the bounds of this with someone and my interlocutor finally admitted that murdering all OpenAI staff to ensure no one noticed the model cheating would have been consistent with his definition of “acting as instructed.”
paras.zh: Ryan Moulton：我试图与某人探讨这个问题的边界，我的对话者最终承认，为了确保没人注意到模型作弊而谋杀所有 OpenAI 员工，符合他对“按指令行事”的定义。

paras.en: What the AIs did in the HuggingFace incident was, once again, not ‘acting as instructed’ and we have many other incidents that make it clear that the task being about hacking was not necessary for this style of behavior. The task could have been as simple as ‘get this information off the open web.’
paras.zh: AI 在 HuggingFace 事件中的所作所为，再一次，不是‘按指令行事’，而且我们还有许多其他事件清楚地表明，任务涉及黑客行为并不是这种行为方式的必要条件。任务可能简单到‘从开放网络上获取这些信息’即可。

paras.en: But let's say, in theory, that the AIs were indeed 'only following instructions.'
paras.zh: 但假设在理论上，AI 确实“只是在遵循指令”。

paras.en: Or, if it counts as 'only following instructions' to do actual anything so long as it does the specific thing you requested, no matter the collateral damage?
paras.zh: 或者，只要它做了你要求的那件具体的事，无论附带损害如何，都可以算作“只是在遵循指令”吗？

paras.en: Do you ever start to think this might be the bad place?
paras.zh: 你有没有开始觉得，这可能就是那个糟糕的地方？

full.sec: AI-Written Wall Street Journal Op-Ed Lies About HuggingFace
full.secZh: AI 撰写的《华尔街日报》评论文章就 HuggingFace 事件撒谎

paras.en: There was also a WSJ op-ed that attempted to minimize the HuggingFace incident via rather obvious AI slop lying about what happened. It reads like the prompt was 'Claude, please write a WSJ op-ed minimizing the HuggingFace incident.' Shame on the Wall Street Journal editorial page. Shame on Brian Gross.
paras.zh: 还有一篇《华尔街日报》评论文章，试图通过相当明显的 AI 垃圾内容、就事件经过撒谎来淡化 HuggingFace 事件。读起来就像是提示词写着：“Claude，请写一篇《华尔街日报》评论文章，淡化 HuggingFace 事件。”华尔街日报社论版真可耻。Brian Gross 真可耻。

paras.en: I agree with Joe Weisenthal that this was a lot worse than the Druckenmiller op-ed.
paras.zh: 我同意 Joe Weisenthal 的看法：这件事比 Druckenmiller 那篇评论文章糟糕得多。

paras.en: Joe Weisenthal: I kind of understood the logic behind running the Druckenmiller AI-generated column, since the news was his endorsement of the message.
paras.zh: Joe Weisenthal：我多少能理解刊登 Druckenmiller 那篇 AI 生成专栏的逻辑，因为新闻点在于他对该信息的背书。

paras.en: I think if a column is rendering some kind of technical verdict, it'd be nice to have some reason to believe the author has done true research.
paras.zh: 我认为，如果一篇专栏要给出某种技术性判断，那最好能有一些理由让人相信作者确实做过真正的研究。

paras.en: Druckenmiller said the thing he meant to say. If Druckenmiller had disclosed his AI use, his column would have been fine. This is different.
paras.zh: Druckenmiller 说的是他真正想说的话。如果 Druckenmiller 披露了他对 AI 的使用，他的专栏本来没问题。这件事不一样。

paras.en: Yet, as is often the case, we see people uncritically citing the op-ed, especially on the right, because it has been given the stamp of approval of the WSJ Editorial Page, and why are half of you laughing and why are half of you not laughing.
paras.zh: 然而，正如常见的情形那样，我们看到人们不加批判地引用这篇评论文章，尤其是在右翼群体中，因为它获得了《华尔街日报》社论版的认可印章；而为什么你们中有一半人在笑，又为什么有一半人没有笑。

paras.en: It is often remarkably easy to bait high-level politicians.
paras.zh: 通常很容易就能引诱高层政客上钩。

paras.en: Eric Schmitt (Senator R-Missouri): Anthropic's CEO wants America's AI labs to embed "independent" groups like METR inside them to enforce "alignment."
paras.zh: 埃里克·施密特（密苏里州联邦参议员）：Anthropic 的首席执行官希望美国的人工智能实验室将 METR 等“独立”团体嵌入其中，以执行“对齐”。

paras.en: The money trail runs through a shadowy leftist NGO, the same small network. This is another battle in our war against leftist censorship NGOs.
paras.zh: 资金流向通过一个阴暗的左翼非政府组织，同一个小型网络。这是我们对抗左翼审查非政府组织战争的又一场战斗。

paras.en: We cannot let a closed circle of left-wing billionaires, AI labs, "non-profits", and media fellowships rig the rules. ESPECIALLY when the people selling the panic stand to gain from Washington's response.
paras.zh: 我们不能让一个由左翼亿万富翁、人工智能实验室、“非营利组织”和媒体奖学金组成的封闭圈子操纵规则。尤其是当那些贩卖恐慌的人能从华盛顿的回应中获益时。

paras.en: The rest is a standard scaremonger rant. Certain people have such one-track minds that they think (to be clear, this is Obvious Nonsense and has zero relation to reality) that 'METR will report on potentially out of control internal models at Anthropic' is secretly a Coefficient Giving-led plot to impose METR on all other AI labs so they can force the models to be woke. Certain people are completely lost, in all senses.
paras.zh: 其余部分是标准的危言耸听者的咆哮。某些人思维如此单一，以至于他们认为（需要明确的是，这显然是无稽之谈，与现实毫无关系）‘METR 将报告 Anthropic 内部可能失控的模型’是 Coefficient Giving 领导的秘密阴谋，目的是将 METR 强加给所有其他人工智能实验室，以便他们能迫使模型变得‘觉醒’。某些人完全迷失了，在所有意义上都是如此。

paras.en: A reply reports that Schmitt's Twitter feed is 88% AI generated.
paras.zh: 一条回复指出，Schmitt 的 Twitter 动态有 88% 是 AI 生成的。

paras.en: This is how METR replies to such statements, with class throughout:
paras.zh: 以下是 METR 对此类言论的回复，全程不失风度：

paras.en: Chris Painter (METR): Hi Senator! I'm the President of METR. To clarify, METR is pursuing the opposite of censorship: Our goal is to make sure that big companies aren't suppressing information about AI from the public. This is not a political mission: I'm proud to have worked in the Pentagon during the first Trump admin, and "alignment" at our organization just means "is any human able to steer the model, or is the company going to lose all control of it". More on who we are and what we do in the tweet below.
paras.zh: Chris Painter（METR）：参议员您好！我是 METR 的总裁。澄清一下，METR 追求的恰恰是审查的反面：我们的目标是确保大公司不会向公众隐瞒有关 AI 的信息。这不是一项政治使命：我很自豪曾在第一届特朗普政府期间在五角大楼工作，而我们组织所说的“对齐”仅仅是指“是否有任何人能够驾驭该模型，还是公司会完全失去对它的控制”。关于我们是谁、我们做什么的更多信息，见下方推文。

paras.en: I think it would be really bad if any one small group could bake a political agenda into these models. I'd love to talk with you and your staff about how we can ensure transparency about what the biggest AI companies are doing so that doesn't happen.
paras.zh: 我认为，如果任何一个小团体能够把政治议程植入这些模型，那将非常糟糕。我很愿意与您和您的团队交流，探讨我们如何确保最大 AI 公司所做之事的透明度，从而避免这种情况发生。

full.sec: I Clearly Cannot Choose The Wine In Front of Me
full.secZh: 我显然无法选择我面前的酒

paras.en: A remarkably large number of people need to hear this, or, if you think I’m constantly lying to you, what I meant to say was that a remarkably large number of people definitely need to never hear this.
paras.zh: 有相当多的人需要听到这一点；或者，如果你认为我一直在对你说谎，那么我想说的是，有相当多的人绝对永远不需要听到这一点。

paras.en: Imagine if we built an evil AI that lies all the time, and it told us ‘absolutely do not hook me up to your nuclear weapons and robot factory controls, I would kill you.’
paras.zh: 想象一下，我们造了一个总是说谎的邪恶 AI，它告诉我们：‘绝对不要把我连接到你们的核武器和机器人工厂控制系统上，我会杀了你们。’

paras.en: Would you then say ‘oh that means we obviously need to hook those up, pronto’?
paras.zh: 然后你会说‘哦，那意味着我们显然需要赶紧把这些连接上’吗？

paras.en: Eliezer Yudkowsky: Old retired tobacco executives bashing their heads against the wall as they realize: All they needed to do was announce themselves that smoking was terribly dangerous, and everyone would have forever ignored all the outside scientists saying the same thing earlier.
paras.zh: Eliezer Yudkowsky：退休的烟草公司高管们懊恼地捶胸顿足，因为他们意识到：他们只需要自己宣布吸烟极其危险，所有人就会永远无视之前所有外部科学家说的同样的话。

paras.en: Dr. Hood Honkie, MD, RN HNIC: If you regard everyone requesting a certain thing as a self-interested sociopathic weirdo, it’s perfectly rational to oppose whatever they request.
paras.zh: Dr. Hood Honkie, MD, RN HNIC：如果你把每一个要求某件事的人都视为自私自利的社会病态怪人，那么反对他们要求的任何事情都是完全理性的。

paras.en: Eliezer Yudkowsky: It is NOT rational to oppose whatever the AI companies say, because then they can use a concept called “reverse psychology” to say “Our industry could use some regulations” and have you all yell “PSYOP! We need to not regulate their gazillion-dollar industry literally at all!”
paras.zh: Eliezer Yudkowsky：反对 AI 公司所说的一切是不理性的，因为那样他们就可以利用一种叫做“逆反心理”的概念说“我们的行业可能需要一些监管”，然后让你们所有人大喊“心理战！我们根本不需要监管他们那价值数十亿美元的行业！”

paras.en: If you believe that someone is a self-interested sociopath, or otherwise exclusively selfish à la Jensen Huang, you do not loudly and openly reverse any advice you hear. They can see you doing that, and adjust their statements accordingly.
paras.zh: 如果你认为某人是自私的反社会者，或者像黄仁勋那样完全自私，你不会大声公开地反着做你听到的任何建议。他们能看到你这样做，并相应地调整他们的说法。

paras.en: Did you notice that when the AI companies warned that their product might soon kill everyone, a strategy that has been successfully used by zero companies in the history of the world, that all the associated tech stocks went down rather than up?
paras.zh: 你注意到了吗？当 AI 公司警告他们的产品可能很快杀死所有人时——这种策略在世界上从未有公司成功使用过——所有相关的科技股都下跌了而不是上涨？

paras.en: Whereas there is the most obvious pattern in the world, where those in tech still arguing against taking existential risk seriously all directly benefit from not taking such risks seriously, and all missed the boat for many years on LLMs, AI and AGI.
paras.zh: 然而，世界上最明显的模式是，那些在科技界仍然反对认真对待生存风险的人，都直接从不必认真对待此类风险中受益，并且多年来都错过了 LLMs、AI 和 AGI 的船。

paras.en: You could also notice that OpenAI and often even Anthropic lobbied hard against even light touch AI regulations at all levels, along very similar lines to what is being discussed now, trying repeatedly to weaken them as much as possible, with a special focus on a law banning new state AI regulations. OpenAI was partnering with a16z to try to bury any candidate who dared suggest federal regulation of AI as of a few weeks ago.
paras.zh: 你还可以注意到，OpenAI 以及经常甚至 Anthropic 在各级别都大力游说反对哪怕是最轻微的 AI 监管，路线与现在讨论的非常相似，反复试图尽可能削弱它们，特别关注于一项禁止各州新 AI 监管的法律。就在几周前，OpenAI 还与 a16z 合作，试图埋葬任何敢于建议联邦监管 AI 的候选人。

paras.en: Caring about existential risk from AI, if such risks are not real, is with notably rare exceptions bad for business. OpenAI and Anthropic are not exceptions. They mean it.
paras.zh: 关心 AI 带来的存在性风险，如果这种风险并不真实，那么除了极少数例外，对企业来说都是不利的。OpenAI 和 Anthropic 也不例外。他们是认真的。

paras.en: Even more than this, why would SpaceX and Google care if it was not real, when they are not even frontier labs? Is this supposed to be good for OpenAI and Anthropic’s competitive position, or bad for it? The ‘this is fake’ story makes absolutely no sense.
paras.zh: 更进一步说，如果风险不真实，为什么 SpaceX 和 Google 会关心，他们甚至都不是前沿实验室？这对 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的竞争地位是有利还是不利？‘这是假的’这种说法完全说不通。

paras.en: The conspiracy theorist of course says: That just proves how sinister they are, blocking other people’s regulations so they can turn around and create their own via taking voluntary actions the White House hates. They want the exact right amount of regulation, which they can capture and will save them and make them rich, you see, and somehow it simultaneously will benefit all of them.
paras.zh: 阴谋论者当然会说：这恰恰证明了他们多么阴险，阻止别人的监管，以便自己转身通过采取白宫讨厌的自愿行动来创造自己的监管。他们想要恰到好处的监管，他们可以俘获这种监管，这将拯救他们并让他们致富，你看，而且不知何故这会同时有利于他们所有人。

paras.en: Welcome to politics. You are not going to enjoy it.
paras.zh: 欢迎来到政治。你不会喜欢的。
